events.text: The tablets of {bb_house} are older than the roof over them. The eldest of the disciples holds the bowl while you say it aloud, so that every junior in the hall can hear: the {bb_art} stays inside these walls. Nobody here says anything. One of the younger ones looks at the door, and then at you, and then at the floor.

choices.text: Look at that one until they look up

effects.log: They look up, in the end. Neither of you says anything, and you both remember it.

choices.text: Tell them why, as plainly as you can

effects.log: You tell them what was lost the last time an art walked out of a house. Some of them believe you. Teaching goes on the next morning, a little quieter.

events.text: You write it into the family register yourself, under your own name, where your grandchildren will have to read it: the {bb_art} belongs to the blood of {bb_house}. Your eldest aunt reads it over your shoulder. "That is a thing that ends friendships," she says. It is not an objection. She only thought you should know.

choices.text: Blot it and close the book

effects.log: You blot it and close the book. The aunt pours the tea. It is, you notice, not any colder than usual.

choices.text: Ask her who it ended, last time

effects.log: She tells you. It takes the rest of the afternoon, and there is a name in it you had always been told died of a fever.

events.text: The branch families come in from three provinces for it, because a dynasty does nothing without an audience. They stand before the tablets of {bb_house} in their good silk and hear that the {bb_art} is the blood's now, and theirs only as long as they stay. Afterward, in the yard, you can tell by how quietly they are talking that they have understood.

choices.text: Walk out among them and let them see you

effects.log: You cross the yard slowly. The talk stops wherever you are and starts up again behind you. That is what you came out for.

choices.text: Have the wine sent out, and stay inside

effects.log: They drink your wine. By morning the cousins have decided that it was the elders' idea, which suits everyone.

events.text: They read it out at the morning assembly, between the duty roster and a complaint about the kitchens: the {bb_art} is bound to the blood of {bb_house}. Anyone who has it keeps it. Anyone who leaves keeps it too, in their head, and will not use it where anyone can see. The senior next to you has stopped breathing through their nose. You know the {bb_art}. Everyone knows you know.

choices.text: Bow with the rest

effects.log: You bow with the rest. It does not cost anything today. You make a note of that.

choices.text: Ask, aloud, what happens to someone who forgets

effects.log: The room goes very still. "Someone goes to remind them," says the elder reading, without looking up. "It is a short conversation. They have had practice."

events.text: The steward finds you in the guest hall and tells you in person, which is the courtesy, and with two retainers behind him, which is the point. The {bb_art} is bound to the blood of {bb_house} from today. You learned it at their table. Nobody is asking for it back. They only want it understood that you are not family, and that the road out of here has people on it.

choices.text: Thank him for telling you

effects.log: You thank him. He looks a little disappointed. He had a second speech ready, and he takes it away with him.

choices.text: Ask whose idea this was

effects.log: He smiles and does not answer, and that is how you learn it was somebody who has been watching you for a while.

events.text: {npc} sits down across from you uninvited, puts a folded page from a family register on the table, and turns it so that you can read it. It has the {bb_art} on it, and the name of {bb_house}, and your own name under that. "You were there when it was bound," {he} says, quite kindly. "You left. Now you fight with it in the open. They would like you to stop."

choices.text: Agree to put it away

effects.log: You give your word across the table. {npc} folds the page up again and leaves it with you, in case you should forget.

choices.text: Tell {him} to come and take it

ok.log: {npc} gets up off the floor slowly, and picks up the page, and looks almost relieved. "I will tell them," {he} says. "They will send me again."

fail.log: {npc} stands over you and does not hurry. "I will tell them you were asked," {he} says, and steps over your legs on the way out.

choices.text: Pay for what it taught you

effects.log: You count it out on the table. {npc} counts it again, writes you a receipt, and puts a line through your name. Nobody has ever been so polite about it.

events.text: You know the walk before you know the face: every child of {bb_house} is taught to walk like that. {npc} stops ten paces off on the empty road and says it the way {he} must have said it to others. "The {bb_art} is bound to the blood, and you are not of it any longer. You may keep it in your head. You may not keep it in your hands."

choices.text: Put it away, for now

effects.log: You nod. {npc} nods back, and then stands there until you have gone around {him}. It is a very long road, after that.

choices.text: Show {him} what your hands remember

ok.log: {npc} ends up in the ditch, and laughs, once. "You always were good," {he} says. "It was never about that."

fail.log: {npc} walks like that for a reason. You find it out on your back, looking at the sky, with {his} heel on your wrist.

choices.text: Ask what the house would take to forget it

effects.log: "More than you think," says {npc}, and names it. It is exactly what you have been saving. They have always kept very good books.

events.text: There is no page on the table this time. {npc} has come by the front gate, at noon, in front of whoever cares to watch. "You were asked," {he} says, loud enough to carry. "You went on using the {bb_art}. {bb_house} sends its regards, and me."

choices.text: Meet {him} in the open

ok.log: {npc} goes down in front of the same people {he} wanted to see it. You almost feel bad. They will have to write that in the register, too.

fail.log: You go down in front of the same people you were keeping it from. {npc} waits for you to get your breath back, and tells you again, in case you missed it.

choices.text: Put it away, and say so in front of them

effects.log: You say it where they can all hear. It costs more than the fight would have. {npc} bows, and goes.

events.text: Your door is open, and you did not leave it open. {npc} is sitting at your own table, with your own tea, and has taken the seat that faces the door. "They will keep sending me," {he} says. "I would rather they stopped. You could do something about that. Or I could. Please finish what you were doing first. There is no hurry, and {bb_house} has sat through worse."

choices.text: Finish your tea, and then finish this

ok.log: You break the table and a good deal else. {npc} leaves by the window, and sends a very correct note about the tea.

fail.log: {npc} does not break anything but you. {He} rinses the cup before {he} goes.

choices.text: Ask for {his} price, and the house's

effects.log: It is a large number and {he} has it ready. You pay it. {He} seems sorry to be going, and takes the cup with {him}.

events.text: The bed has been made, very neatly, and {npc} is not in it. There is a note on the pillow in a hand you taught. It does not apologise. It says that the {bb_art} was given to {him} before it was ever bound, and that {he} would like to see what else there is. The elders of {bb_house} are already outside your door. They have not knocked yet.

choices.text: Send your people after them

effects.log: You open the door and give the order. Nobody asks you if you are sure. You had rather hoped that somebody would.

choices.text: Go after them yourself

ok.log: You catch up with {npc} at the second ferry. You talk until the boat has left twice. {He} comes home, not because you were right, but because you came.

fail.log: You catch up with {npc} at the second ferry. You say all of it. {He} hears you out, and gets on the boat, and you stand there with the elders' question still to answer.

choices.text: Let them go, and lift the binding

effects.log: You open the door and say it to their faces. The arguing goes on for a month. Somewhere on the road, {npc} never finds out how close it was.

events.text: A merchant mentions it, of all people, over the price of salt: there is a young fighter on the east road working for coin, in a style seen only in one family. The merchant describes the {bb_art} quite well, with no idea whose table this is. It is {npc}, and {he} has been gone since the thaw, and everyone in {bb_house} knew but you.

choices.text: Send your people after them

effects.log: You finish the talk about salt. You see the merchant to the gate. Then you send for the men who do this.

choices.text: Go after them yourself

ok.log: You find {npc} in the third town you try, with a split lip, counting {his} winnings. {He} looks up and is suddenly very young. You walk home together, and neither of you mentions it again.

fail.log: You find {npc} in the third town you try. {He} is doing very well. {He} buys you tea, and it is the worst tea of your life, and you go home alone.

choices.text: Let them go, and lift the binding

effects.log: You send the merchant away with a good price on the salt. The next morning you strike the line from the register yourself. It is harder to do than the binding was.

events.text: Two old men from the ancestral hall have come a long way to stand in your yard and not quite look at you. The head of the house is tired, they say. There are people who still speak well of your line. The tablets have been asked, in the way that tablets are asked, and the seal is yours if you will have it: the lands, the feuds, the ledger, everything that comes with the name. They will wait, but not long.

choices.text: Take the seal

effects.log: You say yes. They bow lower than you had expected, and then, a little sooner than you had expected, they start telling you what is wrong.

choices.text: Not now. Let the head keep the seat

effects.log: They do not argue. They drink the tea, they look around at what you have instead, and they leave. They will ask again in ten years, if anyone is left to ask.

events.text: The letter is in the old form, on the house's paper, sealed in the colour you only ever saw on funeral days. The head of your blood will step aside, if you will come. The elders have counted, and you are the one they can stand. You have read it three times. It does not say what happens to what you have built here. It does not need to: a house takes all of you, and the seal does not come off at night.

choices.text: Go home and take the seat

effects.log: You write back the same day. There are things you will miss. You find out what they are later, and one at a time.

choices.text: Send it back, with respect

effects.log: You send it back with your respect and a very good gift. The elders will take the gift, and they will write to you again in ten years.
